item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem:
This graph shows the number of suits and coats sold each month.

[Image: Line graph of suits and coats sold each month]

According to the information in the graph, during which two-month period does the greatest increase in coat sales occur?

A line graph plotted on a grid. The vertical axis is labeled "Number Sold Each Month" with grid lines at multiples of 50 from 0 to 500. The horizontal axis lists the months: Jan, Feb, Mar, Apr, May, Jun, Jul, Aug, Sep, Oct, Nov, Dec. A legend shows a dashed line for "Coats" and a dotted line for "Suits".

Data points for Coats (dashed line):
- Jan: 350
- Feb: 300
- Mar: 250
- Apr: 250
- May: 200
- Jun: 150
- Jul: 100
- Aug: approximately 135
- Sep: 150
- Oct: 200
- Nov: 450
- Dec: 350

Data points for Suits (dotted line):
- Feb: 0
- Mar: 100
- Apr: 150
- May: 200
- Jun: 400
- Jul: 500
- Aug: 450
- Sep: 150
- Oct: 50
- Nov: 0

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: A graph of soft drink sales for cherry cola and lemon cola by year and number of cans in millions.]

The graph shows the sales of two types of soft drink over 4 years. If the sales trends continue for the next 10 years, determine the year in which the sales of Cherry Cola will be the same as the sales of Lemon Cola.
reference_items.figure_description:
A vertical bar graph titled "Soft Drink Sales".
The vertical axis is labeled "Number of cans\n(millions)" with grid marks and horizontal lines at intervals of 10 from 0 to 60.
The horizontal axis is labeled "Year" with four years: 1998, 1999, 2000, 2001.
A legend shows:
- White box: Cherry Cola
- Solid black box: Lemon Cola

For each year, there is a pair of adjacent bars (Cherry Cola on the left, Lemon Cola on the right):
- 1998: Cherry Cola bar reaches 10; Lemon Cola bar reaches 40.
- 1999: Cherry Cola bar reaches 20; Lemon Cola bar reaches 45.
- 2000: Cherry Cola bar reaches 30; Lemon Cola bar reaches 50.
- 2001: Cherry Cola bar reaches 40; Lemon Cola bar reaches 55.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
The graph below shows the humidity in a room as recorded on a certain morning.

[Image: Graph of Humidity in Room]

On the morning shown in the graph, how many times between 6 a.m. and 12 noon was the humidity exactly 20 percent?
reference_items.figure_description: A line graph titled "Humidity in Room". The vertical axis is labeled "Percent Humidity" with horizontal grid lines and markings at 10, 20, 30, 40, and 50. The horizontal axis is labeled "Time (a.m.) in hours" with vertical grid lines and markings at 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, and 12 noon. A continuous curve starts at (6, 5), rises through (7, 20) to a peak at (8, 40), then decreases passing through (9, 30) and (10, 20) to a minimum of about 14 between 10 and 11, then rises passing 20 between 11 and 12, reaching 25 at 12 noon. The curve intersects the horizontal line for 20 percent humidity at three points: at 7 a.m., at 10 a.m., and between 11 a.m. and 12 noon.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
The table shows the temperatures at various times on a certain day.

| Time | 6 a.m. | 9 a.m. | Noon | 3 p.m. | 6 p.m. |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| Temperature °C | 12 | 17 | 14 | 18 | 15 |

A graph, without a temperature scale, is drawn. Of the following, which could be the graph that shows the information given in the table?
reference_items.figure_description:
Four line graphs, labeled A, B, C, and D, each with a vertical axis labeled "Temperature (°C)" without numbers or tick marks, and a horizontal axis labeled "Time" with five evenly spaced tick marks labeled "6 a.m.", "9 a.m.", "Noon", "3 p.m.", and "6 p.m.".
- Graph A: The line begins at a low point at 6 a.m., rises to 9 a.m., rises further to a peak at Noon, drops sharply to a low point at 3 p.m., and rises slightly at 6 p.m.
- Graph B: The line begins at a moderate height at 6 a.m., rises to a peak at 9 a.m., drops at Noon, rises to an even higher peak at 3 p.m., and drops at 6 p.m. to a level higher than the value at Noon.
- Graph C: The line starts at a relatively high point at 6 a.m., drops to 9 a.m., rises to a peak at Noon, drops to 3 p.m., and continues downward at 6 p.m.
- Graph D: The line starts at a low point at 6 a.m., rises to 9 a.m., reaches a maximum at Noon, drops at 3 p.m., and drops further at 6 p.m.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
The graph shows the distribution of crops grown in a certain country.

[Image: Pie chart showing the distribution of crops]

According to the information in the graph, which of these statements is true?

options.label: A
options.text: More oats are grown than wheat.

options.label: B
options.text: Corn is more than one-half of the country’s crop.

options.label: C
options.text: Oats are more than one-third of the country’s crop.

options.label: D
options.text: The total crop of oats and wheat is greater than the corn crop.

reference_items.figure_description:
A pie chart showing four sectors labeled with crop types:
- 'Corn': occupies slightly less than half of the circle, spanning from the 12 o'clock position clockwise to approximately the 4:30 position (roughly 135° to 140°).
- 'Oats': adjacent clockwise from Corn, spanning from approximately 4:30 to 7 o'clock (roughly 75°).
- 'Other': adjacent clockwise from Oats, spanning from approximately 7 o'clock to 8 o'clock (roughly 30°).
- 'Wheat': adjacent clockwise from Other to Corn, spanning from approximately 8 o'clock to 12 o'clock (roughly 115° to 120°).
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

guessing.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's guessing (lower asymptote) parameter c: the probability that a student of very low ability answers it correctly, such as by guessing among the options? Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
